name: Synopsys
thesis: Synopsys — the largest EDA software + design-IP vendor, now also systems/multiphysics simulation via the closed Ansys acquisition. Pure picks-and-shovels on AI: every AI accelerator, custom ASIC, and chiplet has to be designed, verified, and signed off on Synopsys/Cadence tools — independent of which chip or model wins. The bet: as AI token consumption AND token/model variety explode, the world designs (a) more chips and (b) a wider variety of more complex chips (hyperscaler custom silicon, edge AI, chiplets), and design complexity per chip rises super-linearly — all of which expands EDA/IP TAM and tool intensity per design. The signals: (1) revenue compounds low-double-digit organically (~15% for years; reported FY26 growth will look higher with a full year of Ansys), (2) the ~$11.4B RPO (~1.6x revenue) keeps growing — multi-year EDA contracts are the forward demand signal, (3) design-IP and AI-driven verification (where complexity bites hardest) outgrow the core, (4) margins hold/expand once Ansys integration amortization normalizes (FY25 GAAP operating margin 13% is deal-depressed; non-GAAP ~38%, FCF margin ~19%). Rational duopoly with Cadence — both win as the design pie grows; pricing power is structural. Competitive reality: the risks are customer concentration in a handful of hyperscalers/foundries, the Ansys integration, and the China/export-control overhang on EDA — the macro wildcard.
key_driver: EDA + IP revenue growth and RPO/backlog expansion — design activity x rising complexity per design as chip variety grows

tier_1_kpis.name: Revenue YoY Growth (USD)
tier_1_kpis.current: +15.1% FY25 ($7.05B); steady ~15% for years — FY26 elevated by full-year Ansys
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: <8% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (design demand stalling, ex-Ansys-distortion)

tier_1_kpis.name: Remaining Performance Obligations (RPO)
tier_1_kpis.current: $11.4B FY25 (~1.6x revenue) — the forward design-demand signal
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: RPO declines YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (customers pulling back on multi-year design commitments)

tier_1_kpis.name: Gross Margin (GAAP)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: <72% for 2 consecutive Qs (pricing power / mix erosion)

tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Non-GAAP operating margin < 30% (integration not delivering operating leverage)

tier_2_kpis.current: Track separately — IP is where rising chip variety/complexity bites hardest (backfill)

nuance.bear_case: Reported growth is muddied by the Ansys acquisition (inorganic boost to revenue, GAAP-margin drag from amortization) — the market may misjudge true organic momentum for a year. EDA demand is downstream of semiconductor R&D budgets; an AI-capex digestion cycle or a hyperscaler pulling custom-silicon spend would hit RPO. Customer concentration is high (foundries + a few hyperscalers), and China/export controls can strand a non-trivial revenue slice overnight.
nuance.adversarial_take: 'Picks-and-shovels' is the consensus AI-infra trade — SNPS already trades at a premium multiple, so the thesis isn't contrarian; it's a bet that the multiple holds while ~15% organic growth + Ansys cross-sell compounds. The duopoly is real, but so is the valuation.
nuance.stress_test: If organic revenue growth falls below 8% AND RPO declines YoY, the 'more/more-complex chips' demand thesis is breaking regardless of the AI headlines.

competitive_watchlist: Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) — the rational duopoly partner
thesis_breakers_qualitative: Organic revenue growth below 8% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (ex-Ansys distortion)
RPO declines YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (forward design demand contracting)
Non-GAAP operating margin fails to recover toward the high-30s post-Ansys integration
China/export-control action stranding a material revenue slice
A hyperscaler/foundry materially in-sourcing design tooling

break_rules.narrative: Revenue declining YoY for 2 consecutive quarters — outright top-line contraction.
GAAP operating margin negative for 2 consecutive quarters — catastrophic for a structurally profitable EDA name (FY25 ran 13%, Ansys-depressed but positive).
FCF margin below 5% for 2 consecutive Qs — cash conversion broken (catastrophic floor; per-ticker watch is 12%).
Operating cash flow declining >10% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs.

business_model_rules.narrative: Revenue growth below 8% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs — design/chip-variety demand stalling below the historical mid-teens run-rate (note FY26 prints are Ansys-inflated, so a sub-8 reading would be a genuine signal).
RPO declining YoY for 2 consecutive Qs — multi-year design backlog contracting, the leading EDA demand signal. (UNRESOLVED until an RPO-YoY transform KPI is materialized.)
Gross margin below 72% for 2 consecutive Qs — pricing power / mix erosion (FY25 ran 77%).
FCF margin below 12% for 2 consecutive Qs — cash conversion regressing (FY25 ran ~19%).
